correctness.rationale: For any nonempty finite simple H, a point fixed by layer exchange on |PMC(H□K2)| has equal barycentric coefficients on horizontal edge-pairs. Such invariant faces correspond exactly to (T,R), where T is an H-matching and R a set of vertices disjoint from V(T) designating rungs. Every such edge-orbit matching extends to a prism perfect matching by all remaining rungs. Thus the PL orbit-midpoint complex is the ordinary matching complex of fully whiskered W(H), not the vertex-fixed subcomplex. An acyclic matching toggles the pendant at the smallest base vertex not covered by T: along a directed Hasse path, T never grows; within fixed T the toggle cannot be reversed, proving acyclicity. Critical faces are precisely base perfect matchings, p(H) of common dimension n/2−1. The augmented empty/vertex pair leaves a single ordinary 0-cell: contractible if p(H)=0, otherwise p(H) spheres (n=2 handles S0 and p+1 components). Barycentric equivariant Lefschetz fixed-point identity equates reduced trace to reduced fixed-locus Euler characteristic. Independently enumerated every labeled H on n≤4 (75 graphs) from prism perfect matchings, reproducing invariant face-vs-whiskered matching face sets exactly; this bounded experiment corroborates the all-H explicit pairing proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Agarwal–Basak paper studies ordinary perfect-matching complex homotopy of Möbius and circular ladders, not layer-swap geometric fixed points. Other studies treat open polygonal ladders and a broad ordinary matching-complex wedge dichotomy for outerplanar graphs. Their results do not imply the natural exact PL identification or p(H) sphere multiplicities for every (including disconnected/nonouterplanar) base graph. The whiskered-fiber toggle is elementary, but its link to prism equivariant fixed points and exact one-factor extraction remains a natural distinct statement.

value.rationale: A canonical graph involution converts a perfect-matching complex into the ordinary matching complex of a different natural graph. The fixed-locus integral homotopy type exactly enumerates one-factors of arbitrary finite bases, including nonplanar/disconnected graphs; hence the involution Lefschetz trace detects a combinatorial invariant invisible to nonequivariant ladder topology. The structural PL equivalence and all-graph classification have clear standalone use.

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the fixed-point space and reduced alternating trace, not entire prism PMC homotopy nor each graded trace.
